text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Proposed model to cut state aid to municipalities should be changed, Minister of Education Olli-Pekka Heinonen says.
- Finnish Transport Workers' Union (ATK) starts boycotting firms which hire people without working contracts or use illegal labour, chairman Kauko Lehikoinen says.
KAUPPALEHTI

- A decision on a possible merger between power group IVO and oil group Neste will be made soon, and if found rational, the state may force a merger, Trade and Industry Minister Antti Kalliomaki says.
- The construction sector will face a new recession in 1999 if planned state aid cuts are approved and implemented, sector representatives say.

- There are no obstacles to merging state-owned bank Postipankki with state financing institution Vienttoluotto but all options will be studied, says Anssi Rauramo, chairman of Postipankki's supervisory board.
- Finnish timber markets have become strongly centralised due to mergers in the forest industry, shows a report by the Finnish Forest Reseach Insitute (METLA) on data from 1994.
- Finance Ministry will comment on Monday on Statistics Finland's report about its adjustment to data on the level of the state deficit last year.
- Finnish banks are less efficient than Swedish banks' rivalling units in Finland and should reduce staff drastically, study shows.
AAMULEHTI
- The food industry should be able to inform customers more freely about the effects of functional foods and advertise more, sector representatives say.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Restraining consumer demand would be better than cutting state aid to municipalities, says Centre party MP and member of the municipality federation council Mauri Pekkarinen.
- Increasing corporate sponsorship of schools threathens to increase inequality in secondary ecucation, says Erkki Kangasniemi, chairman of the Trade Union of Education (OAJ).
DEMARI
- Heated debate about new cuts in next year's state budget is partly unfounded since much of the reduced spending is due to a revision in the projected state debt servicing costs.
- Temporary working contracts should be made much more expensive for the industry so that they would only be used during production peaks, industry's white-collar workers' union says.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
